# Layouts

A layout decides where every tiled window goes. Each Space has its own layout and keeps its own settings for it (main count, ratio, pane sizes), also across restarts. The layouts you use are listed under `layouts:` in the config; `cycle-layout` and `select-<key>-layout` switch between them.

**You don't need to learn all of this.** Use only the layouts you are really going to use, learn those well, and skip the rest. A good start: read [the window order](#the-window-order) and [the main pane](#the-main-pane), then only the sections of the layouts in your `layouts:`. Come back to the rest when something surprises you.

Part 1 explains the ideas every layout shares, main first. Part 2 shows each layout. Part 3 is a quick reference.

**Reading the diagrams:** each box is a window's tile and its number is the window's place in the window order: 1 is the first window. `·` is a column without a window. Unless a diagram says otherwise, it shows 5 windows, main count 1 and a ratio of 50 %, on a landscape screen.

## Part 1: how main works

### The window order

Every layout works the same way: it takes the tiled windows **in order** and pours them into its panes. The order runs pane by pane: main's windows first, then the first side pane's, then the next one's. Inside a pane it runs top to bottom, or side by side from left to right (from right to left in a Right twin, which is the mirror image).

So a layout never decides *which* window goes where; the order does. The order changes when you:

- swap two windows (`swap-main`, `swap-<direction>`, or dragging one onto another with `mouse-swaps-windows`);
- warp a window into another pane (`warp-<direction>`, `warp-main`, or a Shift-drop with `mouse-warps-windows`);
- open a window, or a window comes back into view (see [arriving and leaving](#windows-arriving-and-leaving)).

Floating windows aren't in the order and take no tile: windows matched by `floating`, the extra windows of apps in `floating-secondary-windows`, windows you float with `toggle-float`, and windows over the [window limit](window-limit.md) when `window-overflow` is `float`.

### The main pane

Main is the pane that holds the first window(s) in the order: the big one, for the work you're doing now. Every other pane is a side pane. Most commands are about main:

- `swap-main` swaps the focused window with main's first window; from main, it swaps back with the window that was there before.
- `focus-main` focuses main's first window.
- `warp-main` moves the focused window into main, and main grows by one.
- `increase-main`, `decrease-main`, `shrink-main` and `expand-main` change how many windows main holds and how big it is (below).

Each layout's name says where main is: Tall **Left**, Wide **Top**, 3Column **Middle**.

### Main count is a maximum

The main count is the **most** windows main may hold, not how many it holds. The HUD and the palette show both as "x of y": 1 of 2 means main holds one window and may hold two.

`increase-main` and `decrease-main` change the maximum. Raising it moves nothing; lowering it below what main holds moves main's extra windows to the first side pane. Main fills up by:

- new windows, while main has room and the side panes are still empty;
- a window arriving with `main-arrival-position: first`;
- a warp into main (`warp-main`, `warp-<direction>`, Shift-drop). A warp into a full main raises the maximum by one; a warp out of main lowers it by one.

Main never empties while there are windows: if its last window leaves, the first side window takes its place.

Tall Left with a maximum of 2. A main window closes, so main holds 1 of 2. What a new window does then depends on `main-arrival-position`:

{{max-tall}}

Two Pane always has one main window. In Column and Row the count is simply the number of main windows: a main window leaving lowers it.

### The ratio

The ratio is main's share of the screen: its width when main is a column, its height when main is a row. It starts at 50 %. `shrink-main` and `expand-main` change it by `window-resize-step` (default 5 %), between 5 % and 95 %, so no pane disappears. With `mouse-resizes-windows`, dragging main's inner edge sets it too.

The side panes share what's left equally. 4Column, Fullscreen, Floating and BSP have no ratio.

### Side panes

Layouts with more than one side pane (3Column, 4Column) share new windows out between them: a new window that doesn't go to main goes to the side pane with the **fewest** windows, and on a tie to the **first** side pane, the one next to main. Inside a side pane, windows split it into equal rows.

3Column Left filling up. With 2 windows the third column stays empty but keeps its width, so main doesn't jump when the next window arrives:

{{fill-3column}}

How many windows each pane holds is remembered per layout (also across restarts), so a warp that makes 3Column 1|2|2 into 1|3|1 stays that way. See [warp](directional-navigation.md#warp).

### Windows arriving and leaving

**Arriving.** `main-arrival-position` decides where a new window goes:

- `last` (default): at the end. It joins main only while main has room and the side panes are empty; otherwise it goes to the side pane with the fewest windows, as above.
- `first`: on top of main, the first window in the order. If main is full, main's last window moves out to the first side pane.

A window coming back into view (unhidden, unminimised, back from another Space, tiled again) arrives the same way, and so does a window warped into main.

**Leaving.** A window that leaves view (closed, quit, hidden, minimised, moved to another Space, floated) shrinks only its own pane; nothing else is rearranged. If that empties a side pane while a later side pane still has windows, the later pane's first window moves over, so a side pane only stays empty when there aren't enough windows.

3Column Left: window 3 closes, then window 2:

{{leave-3column}}

### Twins

Most layouts come in pairs, named by where main is: Tall Left and Tall Right, Wide Top and Wide Bottom, and so on. A layout's **twin** is its exact mirror image: every window lands on its mirror spot, in the same order and the same pane. The side column next to main stays next to main:

{{twins-3column}}

A layout and its twin **share their state**: switching from one to the other (by `select-<key>-layout` or `cycle-layout`) hands over main count, ratio and pane sizes, so the twin shows the same arrangement on the other side. Both need to be in your `layouts:` for that.

| Twins | Mirrored |
|---|---|
| Tall Left ↔ Tall Right | left ↔ right |
| Wide Top ↔ Wide Bottom | top ↔ bottom |
| Two Pane A ↔ Two Pane B | along the screen's long side |
| 3Column Left ↔ 3Column Right | left ↔ right |
| 4Column Left ↔ 4Column Right | left ↔ right |
| Widescreen Tall Left ↔ Widescreen Tall Right | left ↔ right |
| Column Left ↔ Column Right | left ↔ right |
| Row Top ↔ Row Bottom | top ↔ bottom |

3Column Middle, Fullscreen, Floating and BSP have no twin.

### Flip

Three commands rearrange the screen without touching a layout's settings. Each means one thing in every layout:

- **`flip-twin`** shows the layout's mirror image: it switches to the twin, handing over main count, ratio and pane sizes. If the twin is in your `layouts:`, it goes to that entry. If not, the current entry becomes the twin in place: the menu bar title shows the twin, the Layouts menu still lists your `layouts:`, and flipping again (or selecting the listed layout) brings the original back. `layouts:` decides what's shown and cycled, not what exists. 3Column Middle has no twin: there, `flip-twin` swaps the left and right columns, windows and sizes, which needs a window in each.
- **`flip-rows`** reverses the order inside every pane whose windows stack as rows.
- **`flip-columns`** reverses the order inside every pane whose windows sit side by side.

Rows and columns never move a pane, only the windows inside it, and flipping again restores the order. They change the window order itself, so in Tall with main count 2, `flip-rows` makes main's bottom window the first. In BSP they swap the halves of every split along that axis, which mirrors the picture.

Tall Left, its twin, and `flip-rows`:

{{flip-tall}}

Wide Top with main count 2, then `flip-columns`:

{{flip-wide}}

3Column Middle and its `flip-twin`:

{{flip-3column-middle}}

The flip commands have no keys until you bind them; the palette lists them as Flip to twin, Flip rows and Flip columns.

## Part 2: the layouts

### Tall Left / Right

`tall-left`, `tall-right`. Main is a column on one side, as wide as the ratio; the other windows stack in rows in the other column.

{{tall}}

With main count 2, main's windows stack in rows too:

{{tall-m2}}

Main count: a maximum. Ratio: main's width. Warp: between main and the stack. Flip: rows, in main and in the stack.

### Wide Top / Bottom

`wide-top`, `wide-bottom`. Main is a row across the screen, as high as the ratio; the other windows sit side by side in the other row. Tall turned on its side.

{{wide}}

With main count 2, main's windows sit side by side:

{{wide-m2}}

Main count: a maximum. Ratio: main's height. Warp: between the two rows. Flip: columns, in both rows.

### Two Pane A / B

`two-pane-a`, `two-pane-b`. Two tiles, always: main and one secondary. Only one window shows in the secondary tile; every other window waits behind it, and `focus-north` / `focus-south` (west/east on a portrait screen) step through them.

{{two-pane}}

On a landscape screen the tiles sit side by side; on a portrait screen one is above the other. A has main first (left, or top), B has it second (right, or bottom), so B is always A mirrored along the screen's long side:

{{two-pane-portrait}}

Main count: always 1. Ratio: main's share. Warp: swaps, as there's no third place to go. Flip: twin only.

### 3Column Left / Right / Middle

`3column-left`, `3column-right`, `3column-middle`. Main plus two side columns that split into rows. Main is as wide as the ratio; the side columns share the rest equally.

{{3column}}

The first side column is the one next to main; it gets a new window when both have the same number. In 3Column Middle the first side column is the left one:

{{3column-middle}}

3Column Middle has no twin: its mirror image would put the first side column on the right, which is no layout of its own.

Main count: a maximum (main's windows stack in rows). Ratio: main's width. Warp: between columns, into an empty column too. A side column without windows keeps its width (see [side panes](#side-panes)). Flip: rows, in every column; in 3Column Middle, `flip-twin` swaps the side columns.

### 4Column Left / Right

`4column-left`, `4column-right`. Four equal columns, made for a very wide screen (32:9) used like two monitors side by side: main is in the **second** column (Left) or the third (Right), next to the screen's centre, so the first windows land in front of you and later ones go towards the edges. Left and Right say which half main is in.

{{4column}}

Every column is always a quarter of the screen, even without windows, so the order fills from the centre out: main, the column across the centre, the outer column on main's side, then the far edge.

{{4column-fill}}

Main count: a maximum. Ratio: none, the columns are always quarters. Warp: between columns, into an empty column too. Flip: rows, in every column.

### Widescreen Tall Left / Right

`widescreen-tall-left`, `widescreen-tall-right`. Like Tall, but main's windows sit side by side instead of in rows, for wide screens.

{{widescreen}}

With main count 2. In the Right twin, main's first window is at the right edge, the mirror of Left:

{{widescreen-m2}}

Main count: a maximum. Ratio: main's width, shared by main's windows. Warp: between main and the stack. Flip: columns in main, rows in the stack.

### Column Left / Right

`column-left`, `column-right`. One full-height column per window. Main's columns take the ratio's share of the width; the other windows share the rest. The Right twin starts at the right edge.

{{column}}

With main count 2:

{{column-m2}}

Every window gets its own column, so with many windows they get narrow; a [window limit](window-limit.md) helps.

Main count: the number of main columns. Ratio: main's share. Warp: swaps. Flip: columns, main's and the others'.

### Row Top / Bottom

`row-top`, `row-bottom`. Column turned on its side: one full-width row per window, the first on top (Row Bottom: at the bottom). For tall or portrait screens.

{{row}}

With main count 2:

{{row-m2}}

Main count: the number of main rows. Ratio: main's share. Warp: swaps. Flip: rows, main's and the others'.

### Fullscreen

`fullscreen`. Every window fills the screen; the focused one is in front. `focus-cw` and `focus-ccw` bring the others forward in order.

{{fullscreen}}

`toggle-fullscreen` switches a Space between its layout and Fullscreen in place, without Fullscreen being in `layouts:`; going back, every window is in the tile it had.

### Floating

`floating`. Nothing is tiled: windows stay where you put them.

### BSP

`bsp` (Binary Space Partitioning). Each new window splits the window you last focused in half, along its longer side, and a closed window's space goes to the window it was split from. Sizes follow the order windows were opened in; nothing rebalances.

{{bsp}}

BSP has no main pane: main count and ratio don't apply, and a mouse resize doesn't stick (with `snap-back-windows`, the window goes back). A warp moves the window out of its tile and splits the neighbour's.

`flip-columns` swaps the two halves of every side-by-side split, `flip-rows` of every split with one half above the other, so the picture mirrors along that axis. BSP has no twin.

{{flip-bsp}}

Ametrine fixes a few ways BSP strayed from that design:

- **The tree follows the windows actually on screen.** Hidden, closed or moved windows never leave an empty tile, and a window the tree missed still gets one. A hidden app's windows come back at the focused window, not at their old spot.
- **A new window splits the window you last focused**, also when you got there by clicking into another app.
- **Closing one of the first windows doesn't reshuffle the layout:** the windows next to it take over its space.

## Part 3: quick reference

| Layout | Main count | Ratio | Warp | `flip-twin` | `flip-rows` | `flip-columns` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tall Left / Right | maximum | main's width | main ↔ stack | each other | main, stack | — |
| Wide Top / Bottom | maximum | main's height | between the rows | each other | — | both rows |
| Two Pane A / B | always 1 | main's share | swaps | each other | — | — |
| 3Column Left / Right | maximum | main's width | between columns, into an empty one | each other | every column | — |
| 3Column Middle | maximum | main's width | between columns, into an empty one | swaps the side columns | every column | — |
| 4Column Left / Right | maximum | none (quarters) | between columns, into an empty one | each other | every column | — |
| Widescreen Tall Left / Right | maximum | main's width | main ↔ stack | each other | stack | main |
| Column Left / Right | number of main columns | main's share | swaps | each other | — | main, the others |
| Row Top / Bottom | number of main rows | main's share | swaps | each other | main, the others | — |
| Fullscreen | none | none | none | — | — | — |
| Floating | none | none | none | — | — | — |
| BSP | none | none | splits the neighbour's tile | — | top/bottom splits | side-by-side splits |

Commands and settings are described in [configuration-files.md](configuration-files.md); focus, swap and warp in [directional-navigation.md](directional-navigation.md).
